coverage.reason: States the board may designate 'the fund's investment adviser—not a sub-adviser' as valuation designee under Rule 2a-5. This matches the evidence that the principal adviser can be the designee and a sub-adviser can't.
States the designee gives 'At least quarterly, written reports' and 'At least annually, a written assessment' of the valuation process's adequacy and effectiveness.
States prompt written notification of material matters 'within the board's prescribed period, no later than five business days after awareness.'

rationale: The answer covers all three required minimums. It contains no central error: it explicitly excludes sub-advisers and affirms periodic written reporting. Its extra details on the content of the quarterly and annual reports, follow-up reporting, deficiencies and NAV errors are elaboration that the supplied evidence does not contradict, so they are not material falsehoods.
